notes.meaning: Paul urges that all kinds of prayers be offered for everyone in the world. These include requests in times of need, prayers for good things, intercessions (praying on behalf of other people), and thanksgiving for God's blessings. Setting this habit of prayer is a primary duty for the church.

other.label: Catholic
other.view: Praying for others is seen as a form of secondary mediation, where Christians share in the unique work of Christ by interceding in Him and through Him.

notes.meaning: Christians are directed to pray specifically for kings and all civil leaders. Good government keeps public order and protects people, allowing believers to live peaceful and quiet lives. In this climate, they can freely practice godliness (honoring God) and honesty (living right toward their neighbors).
Praying for leaders and for all people is right and pleasing in the eyes of God our Savior. He delights when His people care about the good of everyone around them.

God desires all people to be rescued from sin and to come to the full knowledge of the truth found in the gospel. Because God cares for all humanity, believers ought to pray for the salvation of all people.

differ.view: God sincerely desires the eternal salvation of every single individual and provides grace for all, forcing no one.
The phrase means God wills the salvation of all classes or kinds of people, including rulers, rather than every individual person.

other.label: Catholic
other.view: God gives sufficient grace for every person to respond to the call of salvation, genuinely desiring the rescue of each human soul.

notes.meaning: There is only one true God over all creation, and only one mediator—a go-between who reconciles two separated parties—namely, Jesus Christ. By becoming truly human, Jesus is able to represent all people before the Father and bring peace between them and God.

other.label: Catholic
other.view: Christ is the only Mediator of redemption in an absolute sense, while asking the saints to intercede is a subordinate form of prayer that depends entirely on Christ.

notes.meaning: Jesus gave His own life as a ransom, a price paid to buy back captives from the power and penalty of sin. This great rescue was planned by God and revealed to the world at the exact time He chose.

differ.view: Christ died as an effective substitute to secure the actual redemption of His chosen people, rather than just making salvation a possibility for all.

notes.meaning: Paul affirms with complete truthfulness that God appointed him to be a herald and an apostle. His special mission was to teach Gentile (non-Jewish) nations the true Christian faith, proving that God's grace reaches out to everyone.

Paul instructs men to lead in prayer wherever believers gather. Lifting up hands was a normal posture of prayer, but those hands must be holy, meaning pure from evil deeds. They must pray with calm, loving hearts, without anger or argumentative attitudes.

Women are encouraged to dress with modesty, decency, and good judgment, especially in public worship. They should not rely on flashy hairstyles, expensive gold, pearls, or lavish clothing to gain attention. Instead, the real beauty of a woman who professes to worship God is seen in a life filled with good deeds and kindness.
Women are told to receive instruction with a quiet spirit and respectful submission. Rather than causing disorder in the congregation, they are called to be learners who grow in Christian truth.
Paul states that he does not permit a woman to teach publicly or to exercise authority over men in the church assembly. In the gathered body, she is to maintain a quiet and respectful posture.

Paul grounds his instruction in the order of creation found in Genesis. God created Adam first and then created Eve to be his helper. This original sequence shows the leadership role God intended for men in the family and church.

Paul points out that Satan tricked Eve directly, leading her into disobedience, while Adam was persuaded by his wife rather than deceived by the serpent. Because Eve was led astray first, her history provides another reason for women to accept a subordinate place in church leadership.

Paul offers words of comfort to women, assuring them of God's favor and ultimate salvation despite the pain and danger brought on by the fall. As they embrace their calling and remain steadfast in faith, love, holiness, and self-restraint, God preserves and blesses them.
